title: Peace Key from Reading, Pennsylvania
field_description_long: Ceremonial key to the city of Reading, Pennsylvania. Given to activists by the city mayor during the Great Peace March for Global Nuclear Disarmament in 1986.
image_alt_text: Brass key with a pretzel-shaped handle. The embossed text on the key read "Reading, PA" , " 'The Pretzel Capital of the World' " on one side, and "Mayor Karen A. Miller" on the other.

title: Barometer from the Golden Rule
field_description_long: In 1958, the Golden Rule sailed towards the Marshall Islands to protest nuclear weapons testing. It was the first boat that attempted to disrupt a nuclear test, and this action created publicity and further protests against nuclear testing in the pacific. This barometer from the voyage comes from the Albert Bigelow Papers (DG 076). Bigelow was the captain of the Golden Rule.
image_alt_text: A metal barometer with a glass face. Around the face are numbers to indicate the air pressure; Small lettering in the middle and bottom of the face reads "Selsi", "Holosteric Barometer" , "Copyright 1940 Selsi Co. Inc." and Made in France."

title: Jane Addams' Nobel Peace Prize
field_description_long: The Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to Jane Addams in 1931 for her lifelong dedication to international relations and disarmament. She was the first American woman to receive the honor.
image_alt_text: Gold medal with Alfred Nobel's profile on one side; On the other side are three naked men embracing, they are surrounded by the words "Pro pace et fraternitate gentium" (For peace and fraternity among peoples).
